newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Stockpile cobalt result due by March 27.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Stockpile cobalt result due by March 27.

text.p: Best and final offers in the U.S. government stockpile sale of lower grade cobalt were due at close of business Wednesday, with the outcome published by March 27 as the bids expire that day, Stockpile deputy administrator, Robert O'Brien said.
Bids for 1.1 million pounds were submitted on February 20, and the time taken to evaluate them has prompted some traders to ask the Stockpile to speed up its workings.
There was also some talk, dismissed as bullish hype by some, that the Stockpile's offer was heavily oversubscribed and this was helping to delay the outcome.
"I don't think oversubscription in terms of quantity is the issue," O'Brien said.
The bids, made on a negotiated basis, were all different, complex, and needed time to evaluate, O'Brien added.
On March 31 bids will be due on the Stockpile's sealed bid basis sales of 1 million pounds of higher grade cobalt.
"I think what the delay in the first bid will do is cut down participation in the second bid," one cobalt consumer said.
The delay, coupled with talk of late vessels and Russian problems was all part of the trader "games to talk up the market", the consumer added.

But some traders based their bullishness on good Chinese buying. "They have had a lot of pent up demand after not buying very much in January and February. They have got their financing together now," one trader said.
Average prices for Russian grade metal in the U.S. were quoted at $18.25 to $19.50 per pound, with high grade at $19.50 to $21.50 per pound.
